t: Windward commission recommends against Hawaii County data center bill over vague definition
b: The Windward Planning Commission sent an unfavorable, non-binding recommendation on Bill 170, mainly because it found the data center definition unclear. The Leeward commission was scheduled to review it October 15, then the County Council decides.
iw: Non-binding negative vote, but council still decides on the ban.

t: Windward Planning Commission defers action on Hawaii County data center bill
b: The Windward Planning Commission voted 4-0 to defer Bill 170, which would separate AI data centers from standard data processing facilities in zoning. Next meetings were set for October, with a November 4 deadline to forward a recommendation.
iw: Procedural delay; the ban proposal stays alive.

t: Hawaii County committee advances Bill 170 barring industrial-scale data centers
b: A Hawaii County Council committee voted 8-0 to send Bill 170 to the planning director and planning commissions. It separates industrial-scale data centers from smaller data processing facilities and declares the former not a permitted use. Public-institution facilities are exempt.
iw: Proposed countywide ban on large data centers closes a zoning pathway.

t: Hawaii House adopts resolution seeking working group on large data centers
b: The House adopted HR 196 HD1, asking the State Energy Office to convene a working group on data centers drawing five megawatts or more. It would examine ratepayer protection, grid costs, water and emissions reporting, and report before the 2027 session.
iw: Study could lead to cost-allocation and reporting rules.
